deploy-bot: rollout created id=roll-2969876543 type=config-only env=prod canary=3% -> 15% over 20m change_window=23:45-00:05 PT targets=[routing, timeouts, batching] link: https://go/release/2969876543
sophie.r: starting thread. quick summary: shift regional routing weights toward local az preference, reduce chat timeout 10s->6s, tighten batching for inference endpoints 50ms->15ms. no model changes.
maria_sre: noted. i'll own canary oncall and will escalate if SLOs breach.
kevin_prod: any per-region pinning? apac has a slightly older runtime, prefer pin there?
sophie.r: yes apac stays pinned to runtime v3.8.2 for this window. eu and na get weight adjustment: prefer local region by +12% weight.
alex_eng: added preflight probes for batch-efficiency + request tail latency. rollback if p95 > baseline + 25% or errors > 0.4% or batch-eff < 0.65 for 5m.
observability-bot: Preflight dry-run OK. Baseline metrics: p50=110ms p95=290ms errors=0.09% batch-eff=0.82. Will emit real metrics within 3 minutes of traffic.
kevin_prod: posting short release blurb to infra-ops and account teams.
natalie_pm: will draft release note after canary. planning to schedule a quiet promote window at 09:00 PT tomorrow if all green.
sophie.r: rollback command: `deploy-bot rollback roll-2969876543 --now` practice in staging first. pin command if needed: 
```
/redwood routing pin --region apac-south --version v3.8.2 --reason "compat pin for runtime"
```
maria_sre: oncall monitoring set. i'll watch p95, error-rate, and batch-eff. also watching memory allocs; tight batching can bump mem pressure.
observability-bot: Canary started at 23:45:10 PT -> 3% traffic. Emitting metrics every 60s.
observability-bot: 23:48:12 PT p50=115ms p95=305ms errors=0.11% batch-eff=0.79
kevin_prod: small p95 lift, batch-eff drop within expected. continuing.
observability-bot: 23:55:30 PT canary bumped to 15%. metrics streaming.
observability-bot: 00:00:40 PT p95=365ms (baseline +25%), errors=0.22%, batch-eff=0.70
alex_eng: p95 right at threshold. continue to observe for 5 more minutes.
kevin_prod: cost note: tighter batching increased token cost ~6% on thin requests. flagged to pricing team.
maria_sre: no memory signals. still green on error threshold.
observability-bot: 00:04:10 PT p95=375ms (baseline +29%), errors=0.19%, batch-eff=0.68
alex_eng: still under our abort threshold (+25% was abort point) but creeping close to our secondary alert (+30%). keep eyes.
sophie.r: hold at 15% for now. if p95 crosses +30% or errors >0.4% for 3m, we'll rollback.
kevin_prod: understood. i'll delay full promote until morning if stable.
observability-bot: 00:08:05 PT p95=392ms (baseline +35%), errors=0.42%
maria_sre: triggering rollback now. executing: `deploy-bot rollback roll-2969876543 --now`
deploy-bot: rollback initiated for roll-2969876543 by maria_sre status=ROLLBACK_IN_PROGRESS
observability-bot: rolling metrics: p95 falling back toward baseline.
deploy-bot: rollback complete status=ROLLED_BACK at 00:12:02 PT. canary nodes drained, routing weights restored, apac pin preserved.
sophie.r: thanks team. good catch. i'll open a short postmortem and include a follow-up plan to try a more gradual timeout change and explore alternative batching profile.
natalie_pm: publishing immediate note to #announcements and tagging customer-facing teams. will await postmortem link.
kevin_prod: creating a follow-up ticket to test tighter batching in load-testing env with larger seq distribution.
alex_eng: also adding experiment to try 30ms batching with adaptive microbatching for small requests. will iterate and re-propose a new rollout.
sophie.r: closing thread for now. react with :white_check_mark: when you've read the rollback outcome.
